# browser-pilot

Automation-first browser control for agents.

Flightplan is the companion package for simple, reusable, low-cost automation on top of
browser-pilot: https://github.com/svilupp/flightplan. It will be released immediately after
browser-pilot. Use `bunx flightplan --help` for its interface.

## Getting oriented

- Run `bp --help` to see the routed command tree.
- Run `bp --version` to confirm the CLI build.
- Route by job before picking a command.

## Route by job

- Inspect page state: `bp snapshot`, `bp page`, `bp forms`, `bp text`, `bp targets`, `bp diagnose`
- Act in the browser: `bp exec`, `bp run`
- Capture a human demo: `bp record`
- Analyze behavior over time: `bp trace`
- Exercise voice/media: `bp audio`
- Change browser conditions: `bp env`
- Review structured state: `bp review`
- Discover or invoke page tools: `bp webmcp status|list|call`

## Canonical workflows

Connect to a local or cloud browser:

```bash
bp connect --name dev                              # Local Chrome (default)
bp connect --provider browser-use --name dev       # Cloud browser (recommended when no local Chrome)
bp connect --new-tab --page-url https://app.example.com --cf-access  # Behind Cloudflare Access
```

Inspect and act:

```bash
bp exec -s dev '{"action":"goto","url":"https://example.com"}'
bp snapshot -i -s dev
bp text -s dev --selector main
bp review -s dev --json
bp exec -s dev '[{"action":"click","selector":"ref:e4"}]'
```

Record and derive:

```bash
bp connect --name demo
bp record -s demo --profile automation -f ./artifacts/demo.recording.json
# perform the flow manually, then stop with Ctrl+C
bp record summary ./artifacts/demo.recording.json
bp record inspect ./artifacts/demo.recording.json
bp record derive ./artifacts/demo.recording.json -o ./artifacts/demo.workflow.json
jq . ./artifacts/demo.workflow.json
bp run ./artifacts/demo.workflow.json -s demo
```

`bp record` captures an existing named session; it does not create a named session. `bp record derive` writes browser-pilot workflow JSON for `bp run`. Use Flightplan for simple reusable workflows.

Trace live behavior:

```bash
bp trace start -s dev --timeout 20000
bp trace summary -s dev --view ws
bp trace summary -s dev --view console
```

Voice workflow:

```bash
bp audio setup -s vt
bp exec -s vt '{"action":"goto","url":"https://my-voice-app.com"}'
bp audio check -s vt
bp audio roundtrip -s vt -i prompt.wav --transcribe
bp trace summary -s vt --view voice
```

## Stable expectations

- Local CLI sessions use one browser-scoped daemon by default; CI sets `BROWSER_PILOT_NO_DAEMON=1`
- Closing the final local logical session leaves the daemon reusable; inspect it with `bp daemon list`
- WebMCP tools are page-scoped and must be listed again after navigation

- `bp snapshot -i` returns actionable elements with refs like `ref:e4`
- `bp page` is compact and caches the refs it shows, but it is not an exhaustive action inventory
- `bp text` is the primary command for readable long-form page copy
- `bp exec --json` returns `success`, `totalDurationMs`, and per-step results including `selectorUsed`, `error`, `suggestion`, and `hints` when available
- On a failed testid/id lookup, `bp exec --json` `hints[]` now normalizes dashed/underscored/camelCase intents: an intent like `create-order` (or `create_order` / `createOrder`) can now match an element labeled `Create Order`. Expect richer, sometimes different, testid/id hint suggestions than before 0.1.0
- `bp record summary <artifact>` returns counts, trace summaries, and next-command tips
- `bp trace summary <source> --view <view>` returns a view-specific summary over canonical trace events
- `bp trace export ...` writes events plus derived summaries
- `bp review --json` returns structured business state: headings, forms, alerts, tables, key-values, status labels
- `bp exec --json` with outcome conditions returns `outcomeStatus`, `matchedConditions`, `retrySafe` per step

## Trace-backed steps in exec/run

- `waitForWsMessage`
- `assertNoConsoleErrors`
- `assertTextChanged`
- `assertPermission`
- `assertMediaTrackLive`

## Outcome conditions in exec/run

Any action step can verify its effect with conditions:

- `expectAny`: success if any condition matches
- `expectAll`: success only if all match
- `failIf`: failure if any matches (checked first)
- `dangerous`: never auto-retry on ambiguous outcome

Condition kinds: `urlMatches`, `elementVisible`, `elementHidden`, `textAppears`, `textChanges`,
`networkResponse`, `stateSignatureChanges`, `selectedTab`, `fieldValue`, `checkbox`, `switch`,
`elementEnabled`, `targetCount`, `newTarget`, `urlChanged`, and `fieldChanged`.

Retries respect the dispatch boundary: pre-dispatch failures may retry the action, while
dispatched or uncertain effects are observed and conditions re-evaluated instead of blindly
repeating input. Use `effect` and `dangerous` when the retry policy matters.

Example:

```bash
bp exec -s dev '[
  {"action":"submit","selector":"form",
   "expectAny":[{"kind":"urlMatches","pattern":"*/dashboard*"}],
   "failIf":[{"kind":"textAppears","text":"Error"}],
   "dangerous":true}
]'
```

## Widget actions in exec/run

- `chooseOption`: custom combobox/dropdown selection
- `upload`: file upload with verification
- `review`: structured page state extraction
- `delta`: page change detection

## Anti-rules

- Do not open raw recording artifacts first. Start with `bp record summary`, `bp record inspect`, or `bp trace summary --view ...`
- Do not use `bp trace` to click or fill elements. Use `bp exec`
- Do not use `bp env` as a generic utilities namespace. It is only for browser/session state controls
- Prefer `bp trace tail ...`; `bp listen ...` is compatibility only
- Prefer `--debug`; `--trace` is a legacy alias
- Do not use `bp snapshot` when you need structured business data. Use `bp review`
- Do not use `bp eval` as a first choice. It is an escape hatch for raw JS.
- `waitFor: "networkIdle"` only means transport quiet; follow it with `bp snapshot -i`, `bp text`, `bp review`, or explicit assertions on hydrated apps
- On noisy commerce pages, scope reading with `bp text --selector main` or another container
- `bp review` is strongest on confirmations, detail pages, tables, alerts, and key-values; it is often weak on catalog grids
- After `bp trace start`, begin with `bp trace summary --view session` before you narrow to `console`, `ws`, or `voice`
